record.original_question: Let H be a complex Hilbert space, let C be a conjugation on H, meaning a conjugate-linear isometric involution with C^2 = I and <Cx, Cy> = <y, x>, and let T be a bounded linear operator on H that is C-symmetric, meaning T = C T* C. Can one develop numerical methods based on approximate antilinear eigenvalue problems to compute singular values of concrete complex symmetric operators, such as differential or integral operators? In particular, can this approach be used to compute resolvent norms ||(T - zI)^(-1)|| for specified classes of such operators?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let H be a complex separable Hilbert space, and let C : H → H be a conjugation, i.e., a conjugate-linear map satisfying C² = I and ⟨Cx, Cy⟩ = ⟨y, x⟩ for all x, y ∈ H. A bounded linear operator T on H is called C-symmetric (complex symmetric) if T = C T* C. For such a C-symmetric operator T, the antilinear eigenvalue problem is to find pairs (λ, x) with λ ≥ 0 and x ≠ 0 such that Tx = λ Cx; the nonzero values |λ| arising this way coincide with singular values of T whenever Cx = x̄ in a suitable basis.

Develop numerical methods, based on truncation/Galerkin discretizations of the antilinear eigenvalue problem T x = λ C x, for the effective computation of singular values of concrete classes of bounded C-symmetric operators T (for example, differential operators with appropriate boundary conditions, or integral operators with complex symmetric kernels). In particular, design and analyze such a method to compute, for prescribed z ∈ ℂ outside the spectrum of T, the resolvent norm

  ‖(T − zI)^{-1}‖,

for specified classes of C-symmetric operators, and prove convergence of the proposed approximations as the discretization is refined.
artifact.status_search_result: Antilinear eigenvalue formulations connecting complex symmetric operators to singular value computation are well established (notably via Takagi's procedure and the work of Garcia–Putinar and collaborators), and concrete algorithms have been developed and compared for matrices and certain operator classes. However, a general program of provably convergent antilinear-eigenvalue-based methods for resolvent norms of broad classes of unbounded or operator-theoretic complex symmetric operators (e.g., differential/integral operators) remains an active research direction rather than a fully resolved problem.

status_evidence.title: Complex symmetric operators and applications II
status_evidence.snippet: Antilinear eigenvalue problem Tf=λ\bar f for complex symmetric T, analogous to Takagi's process for singular numbers.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational link between antilinear eigenproblems and singular values for complex symmetric operators.

status_evidence.title: A comparison between the complex symmetric based and classical computation of the singular value decomposition of normal matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm using unitary equivalence of normal matrices to complex symmetric tridiagonal form combined with symmetric SVD.
status_evidence.claim: Concrete numerical algorithms exploiting complex symmetric structure exist for matrices.

status_evidence.title: Norm estimates of complex symmetric operators applied to quantum systems
status_evidence.snippet: Applications of complex symmetric operator framework to norm estimates in quantum systems.
status_evidence.claim: Resolvent/norm estimation for complex symmetric operators is an ongoing applied program.
